pattern.crimePattern: a Nairobi records officer who makes land files disappear kills the clerk who listed the missing files, and drives her body out to a murram pit
pattern.notes: Fictional people, registry and ministry team. Region 8 boss. The registry man (t_registry) is identified as Julius Emojong. In his drawer: the 37 files, Abdia's green notebook, and Joseph Mwenda's working field book, taken from his body twelve years ago. Abdia's letter to Ubah was found in case 77.

ob.text: A family in Isiolo reports their daughter missing since Friday evening: Abdia Golicha (32), records clerk at the Isiolo county land registry. She never came home from work.

facts.text: Abdia Golicha, records clerk at the Isiolo land registry, has been missing since she failed to come home from work on Friday.
The tuk-tuk driver waited at the registry gate from 17:30 to 18:15 as every evening; she never came out.
Her mother: on Thursday Abdia said, "I've found something at work. I'm writing it down." Her fiancé Jattani's family and hers were arguing over the wedding.
Sign-out book, Friday after 17:00: Florence 17:20, Registrar Guracha 17:45, Emojong 19:55 "project vehicle — archive boxes". No sign-out for Abdia.
Galma: every staff member signs the book after 17:00. "I check names, not faces."
Galma: Mr. Emojong came back in at about 18:25, "for something he'd forgotten", and didn't come out again until 19:55.
Galma: at 19:55 Emojong pushed out a trolley with a big archive box. "He said it was going to Nairobi. Abdia? I thought she'd gone at five with the others."
Records ①: Abdia's phone was on the Isiolo mast until 18:41, then switched off. It never moved.
Scan log: sequence 0001–4,812, with 37 numbers missing in the middle of runs.
Index cards: 37 files absent from the shelves, and no dispatch-book entry for any of them leaving.
Registrar's tray: a pad of dispatch notes pre-signed by Guracha with the details blank; three used, typed "Dispatched to Nairobi for digitisation".
Under raking light: on a used dispatch note the typing lies on top of the signature's ink. The form was signed blank and filled in later.
Questioned Documents Lab: all three used notes were typed over signatures made on blank forms, on the team's typewriter ribbon.
The Garba Tula file was withdrawn "for digitisation" on a requisition signed with the officer code J.E./SRO/0331.
Case 40 exhibit: the slip that withdrew FB 4471, Bahati Block 9, eleven years ago, signed with an officer code.

reconstruction.text: Eleven years ago Julius Emojong withdraws Joseph Mwenda's official field book, FB 4471, from the national registry. It never comes back. He keeps something else, given to him to destroy: Joseph's own working field book, taken from his body on the Bahati road.

Three months ago he arrives in Isiolo with a "digitisation team". Files are scanned, the scans deleted, the paper locked in drawer 14, the dispatch notes typed on forms signed blank. Abdia starts a list in a green notebook. On Thursday at 16:10 she hears him on the phone: "Tell the fourth floor the north is clean by month end."

Friday. She stays late, finds the drawer 14 key in the scanner tray and opens the drawer. At 18:25 he comes back for his key and finds her photographing the files. He strikes her with the steel binding punch, switches off her phone at 18:41, and locks her notebook and phone in the drawer.
At 19:00 he buys the vehicle key from Omar. At 19:55 he signs out, "project vehicle — archive boxes", and wheels her out in an archive box on a trolley. His phone leaves the Isiolo mast at 20:20.
At km 32 of the Garba Tula road he leaves her in an abandoned murram pit. He is back on the Isiolo mast at 21:15 and returns the key at 21:30, murram dust on the tyres.

afterVerdict.beat: Abdia's 37 files go back on the Isiolo shelves, each with a new index card in Insp. Halake's handwriting: "Returned. Abdia Golicha's list." The Garba Tula community's registration file is among them. At a community assembly the lease is cancelled; the women's group chair reads Abdia's name out first.
Emojong is charged with Abdia's murder. He says nothing more.

ui.beatNotes: The gap ruler. The scan log scrolls as a long strip of numbers; the player drags a ruler along it and every missing number drops out as a dotted gap. Matching each gap to an index card lights a file-shaped hole on the shelf photo. Thirty-seven holes. After the verdict, Joseph's working field book can be opened page by page.
